newsitem.title: CROATIA: Rain delays start of Croatian beet harvest.
newsitem.headline: Rain delays start of Croatian beet harvest.

text.p: Wet weather is delaying Croatia's sugar beet harvest, expected to yield some 880,000 tonnes this year, an agriculture ministry official said on Tuesday.
"I have been in touch with beet growers and they are waiting for a break in the rain to start the campaign. It could begin around (September 20)," Irena Ljesevic told Reuters.
The rain was reducing sugar content, she said, adding that all the main growing areas in the northeast of Croatia were affected.
After a poor 1995 crop, Croatia imported raw sugar from Hungary to help meet annual needs of just under 140,000 tonnes.
A total of 20,738 hectares were planted to sugar beet this year and the average yield was forecast at 44 tonnes per ha.
Rains in July and August this year helped root growth, boosting yields to roughly 40-60 tonnes per ha when hand picked, minus some 20 pct where machinery is used.
The second beet test, carried out last week, showed sugar content ranging between 11.5 and 15.5 percent, little changed from 1995, the Sugar Beet Institute in Osijek said.
According to its head, Andrija Kristek, sugar content had increased some 0.3-0.5 percent since the first test a fortnight earlier, but was not expected to improve much by harvest time.

"The root needs sunshine and not water any more," Kristek said. "However, since the leaf is well preserved, the beet will not use up sugar to sprout new leaves, so its content could remain at the current 11-13 percent on average."
He put daily yield growth at 250-380 kg/ha.
